title: Roots of Polynomials
summary: Finding all roots uses the Rational Root Theorem to list candidates, synthetic division to peel off factors, and the quadratic formula for what remains. The Fundamental Theorem guarantees $n$ roots (counting complex ones and multiplicity) for a degree-$n$ polynomial.

root/zero.plain: A value where the polynomial is 0.

Fundamental Theorem of Algebra.plain: A degree-$n$ polynomial has $n$ complex roots.

complex roots.in_class: Come in conjugate pairs for real coefficients.

conjugate pair.in_class: Both are roots if one is (real coefficients).

multiplicity.plain: How many times a root repeats.
multiplicity.in_class: Sum of multiplicities equals the degree.

depressed polynomial.plain: What's left after dividing out a root.

factored form.plain: The polynomial written as a product of factors.

concept_sections.heading: The Fundamental Theorem
concept_sections.explanation: A degree-$n$ polynomial has exactly $n$ roots in the complex numbers, counting multiplicity. Real ones are x-intercepts; others come in complex conjugate pairs.

concept_sections.heading: The Rational Root Theorem
concept_sections.explanation: Possible rational roots are $\pm\dfrac{p}{q}$ where $p$ divides the constant term and $q$ divides the leading coefficient. Test these candidates.
math_steps: List factors of the constant and leading coefficient.

concept_sections.heading: Peeling off roots
concept_sections.explanation: Once a root $r$ is found, divide by $(x-r)$ to get a lower-degree 'depressed' polynomial, then repeat or solve it directly.

concept_sections.heading: Complex conjugate roots
concept_sections.explanation: For real-coefficient polynomials, complex roots always occur in conjugate pairs $a\pm bi$. Finding one gives its partner for free.
math_steps: A complex root implies its conjugate.
They multiply to a real quadratic.

concept_sections.heading: Full factorization
concept_sections.explanation: Combine all roots (real and complex, with multiplicity) to write the polynomial as a product of linear (and irreducible quadratic) factors.

real_world_examples.title: Solving a design equation
real_world_examples.scenario: A volume equation is a cubic.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: The Rational Root Theorem finds a workable dimension, then the rest solves as a quadratic.

real_world_examples.title: Signal frequencies
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Complex conjugate roots correspond to oscillating behavior.

real_world_examples.title: Break-even analysis
real_world_examples.scenario: Profit is a polynomial set to zero.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Its real roots are the break-even quantities.
